title: Differential compatibility of the internal Hom cone comparison
statement: Let C be a small category, J a Grothendieck topology, R a commutative ring sheaf, E,G,I integer-indexed cochain complexes of R-module sheaves, and f:G→I a chain map. Fix the product projections of homComplex_projections_exists. Suppose e_n identifies the degree-n objects of cone(Hom(E,f)) and Hom(E,cone(f)), and its projection to each p-th Hom factor is the sum of the G-part and I-part obtained by the cone projections, Hom-product projections, and internal Hom of the two cone inclusions, exactly as in the Lean statement. Then these e_n commute with the differentials for all adjacent degrees. This statement supplies no degreewise isomorphisms.

source.place: Section 0A8X (the displayed internal Hom differential) and Section 08J7, proof of Lemma 21.35.4 (termwise split sequence argument)

proof.text: For adjacent degrees n and n+1, use the limit clause of homComplex_projections_exists to reduce equality of the two morphisms to equality after each degree-(n+1) product projection. Generalize the assumed component equation over its target indices so that equal integer expressions are handled by their index proofs rather than by casts.

Expand the Hom differential using the differential clause of homComplex_projections_exists, and substitute the assumed component equation in degrees n and n+1. Expand the source cone differential using Mathlib homotopyCofiber.d_fstX and d_sndX, and expand the target cone differential using inlX_d and inrX_d. Apply the map clause of homComplex_projections_exists to Hom(E,f). Functoriality of homObjMap combines consecutive pre- and post-compositions. Its additivity and compatibility with negation in the second variable are proved sectionwise in private helpers; the additivity helper works over a site in universe v and ring and module values in max u v, specializing to the small-site cone calculation. This produces the same G-differential, f, and I-differential terms on both sides.

The remaining source-differential terms match by Int.negOnePow_succ and distribution of composition over subtraction and unit scalar multiplication. After removing compositions with identities, the resulting equation is the additive-group identity -a+b+c-(x+y)=-(a-(-x))+(b+(c-y)), proved by abel in a private helper. Product joint monicity finishes. No joint-monicity assertion for internal Hom of cone projections is needed; no boundedness, product exactness, or extra dependency is used.

proof_origin.place: Sections 0A8X and 08J7; direct calculation using cone inclusions and product projections, formalized by W3.

lean.statement:
theorem homComplex_mappingCone_differential
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u})
    (E G I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R)) ℤ)
    (f : G ⟶ I) :
    let π := Classical.choose
      (homComplex_projections_exists.{u, u, u, u} (C := C) (J := J) (R := R))
    let hf := ((homComplexFunctor (R := R)).obj (op E)).map f
    let K := HomologicalComplex.homotopyCofiber hf
    let cf := HomologicalComplex.homotopyCofiber f
    let H := ((homComplexFunctor (R := R)).obj (op E)).obj cf
    ∀ (e : ∀ n : ℤ, K.X n ≅ H.X n),
      (∀ n p : ℤ, (e n).hom ≫ π E cf n p (p + n) rfl =
        (show K.X n ⟶ SheafOfModules.homObj (R := R) (E.X p) (cf.X (p + n)) from
        HomologicalComplex.homotopyCofiber.fstX hf n (n + 1) rfl ≫
          π E G (n + 1) p (p + (n + 1)) rfl ≫
          SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := R) (𝟙 (E.X p))
            (HomologicalComplex.homotopyCofiber.inlX f (p + (n + 1)) (p + n)
              (by change (p + n) + 1 = p + (n + 1); omega)) +
        HomologicalComplex.homotopyCofiber.sndX hf n ≫ π E I n p (p + n) rfl ≫
          SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := R) (𝟙 (E.X p))
            (HomologicalComplex.homotopyCofiber.inrX f (p + n)))) →
      ∀ n m : ℤ, n + 1 = m →
        (e n).hom ≫ H.d n m = K.d n m ≫ (e m).hom
